clue.text: Chap buttonholing one new Cabinet member

indicators.note: to buttonhole someone is to grab and hold them, so the chap's title holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Mister is the title for a man, a chap
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A man corners a freshly appointed government member for a word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttonholing' puts I (one) and N (new) inside MISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior government official who heads a department sits in the Cabinet.

clue.text: Devious liar sheltered by greatest ethical thinker

indicators.note: something sheltered by another sits inside it, so the reworked letters go within the word for greatest

parts.note: most means greatest in amount

indicators.note: devious means crooked or winding, telling us to twist these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A great moral philosopher shields a crooked fibber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greatest' supplies the outer shell; 'Devious' scrambles the liar into RALI so it fits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone preoccupied with right and wrong, a person who reflects on virtue and preaches it.

clue.text: Write up a song with nautical character

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to pen is to write
a tune is a melody or song

explanation.surface: Instructions to compose a sea shanty for a seafaring personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Write' is a verb here (to pen), and 'up' reads it bottom to top in this down clue, giving NEP.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of the sea is a mythological figure tied to sailors and the ocean.

clue.text: Black book available in discount event

indicators.note: a book available in a shop event is found inside it, so this letter goes within the event's word

parts.note: a sale is an event where goods are sold at reduced prices

explanation.surface: A dark-covered volume turns up cheaply at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available in' puts B inside SALE, after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic and poetic word for the colour black.

clue.text: Claiming tea, when brewed, is hard to see through

indicators.note: brewing mixes ingredients together, so these letters are stirred into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone insisting on tea leaves their motives unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when brewed' rearranges the eleven letters of CLAIMING TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: Something puzzling or mysterious is opaque, its meaning not easily penetrated.

clue.text: Arbiter of morals endlessly scorned, looking foolish

indicators.note: looking foolish suggests something out of shape, telling us to rearrange the remaining letters
without its end, the clue word scorned loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A moral watchdog is mocked and made to look silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops D from SCORNED, and 'looking foolish' rearranges SCORNE.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who suppresses offensive material judges what is fit for public morals.

clue.text: European starts job: conjuring

indicators.note: the single letter starts the next word, so it is placed in front of it

parts.note: a vocation is a calling or job

explanation.surface: A person from Europe begins a new post that involves magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' puts E in front of VOCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling up spirits or memories is summoning them, as a conjuror or medium does.

clue.text: Appear certain about circumstance, for the most part

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for certain goes around the shortened word

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, with its last letter removed

parts.note: a fact is a circumstance or detail of a case

explanation.surface: Certainty about the situation appears to be mostly present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the final T; 'about' wraps the certain word around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To surface is to come up into view, emerging or showing up.

clue.text: Car cylinder

explanation.walkthrough: Roller as a Rolls-Royce is British slang for the luxury car.
explanation.definitionFit: Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce motor; it is also any rotating drum used for pressing or smoothing.

clue.text: Left-over item seen around bar in France, say

indicators.note: the leftover word is seen wrapped around the bar's word, enclosing it

parts.note: a relic is something surviving from the past
a pub is a bar

explanation.surface: An old artefact seen in a French bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'France, say' signals an example: France is a state with an elected head, so the definition is a category.
explanation.definitionFit: France is an example of a state with an elected head rather than a monarch.

clue.text: Crikey! Bar excluding one -must be OK place!

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like crikey

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out, so a letter is removed from the bar's word

parts.note: a rail is a bar
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a bar that must be in a famous Western town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' takes I from RAIL. The OK Corral in Tombstone, Arizona, was the site of a famous 1881 gunfight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for livestock; the most famous one is the OK enclosure of Wild West legend.

clue.text: Verminous creature long associated with river

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A pest that has long lived by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: A small parasitic insect infesting hair or skin is classic vermin.

clue.text: Handle team badly, main games being thrown

indicators.note: matches being thrown are deliberately lost, and here letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A manager mishandles a squad, with the big matches deliberately lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being thrown' rearranges MAIN GAMES.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something incompetently is to direct it poorly, as a bad coach would a side.

clue.text: Criminal unlikely to spoil Christmas?

explanation.walkthrough: A Christmas cracker is a paper tube pulled apart at British festive meals; a safe one won't spoil the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A burglar who opens strongboxes; read differently, a party popper that is harmless and won't ruin the festive dinner.

clue.text: Disobey rules, causing problem on flight?

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a flight of stairs, not an air journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To break conventions of behaviour is to misbehave; on a staircase, a stair not aligned with the others is a hazard.

clue.text: Thin stuff — leek?

parts.note: a translucent, very light paper is named after the papery outer layer of an allium such as a leek

explanation.walkthrough: The leek belongs to the onion family, so its thin outer layer suggests the name of the lightweight paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, glossy paper used for copies takes its name from the outer layer of a bulb vegetable.

clue.text: Dagger — left it raised in course of scuffle

indicators.note: in the course of means partway through, so the turned letters sit within the scuffle's word

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight or scuffle

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knife is pulled and held high during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the left-it pair to read TIL in this down clue; a set-to is British for a brief fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short knife with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Member of royalty: value study about new type

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the value word goes around the new letter

parts.note: price is value or worth
to con is to study or learn by heart
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A royal personage is valued and studied as a new sort of figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like a noun but is the verb to con, learn by heart; 'about' wraps the value word round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The husband of a reigning queen holds a royal title, Albert being the best-known example.

clue.text: One election curtailed in China? That's very important

indicators.note: the letters are placed in the friend's word, inside it

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china is a pal
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: curtailed means having the tail cut off, so the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a vote is an election

explanation.surface: A shortened poll in China is said to matter greatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the election word's last letter. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate, so china means friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crucial is central, like the point on which everything turns.

clue.text: Leading officer working to bring in label with regular shape

indicators.note: the officer and working letters together take in the label word between them

parts.note: OC stands for Officer Commanding, the officer in charge
on means working or functioning
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A commander sets about bringing a tag for a geometric figure.
explanation.walkthrough: OC (Officer Commanding) and ON together take the label inside, splitting between the C and the O.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon with equal sides and angles is a regular figure.

clue.text: Tribe member giving cry of pain, one pierced by pole

indicators.note: the cry is pierced, so the pole's word is pushed inside it

parts.note: ow is an exclamation of pain
a jib is a projecting spar or boom on a crane or ship
a means one

explanation.surface: A tribesman cries out in pain when someone is speared by a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: A jib is a spar or boom, so it serves for a pole; the Ojibwa are also called Chippewa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ojibwa are a Native American people of the Great Lakes region.

clue.text: Girl penning Caesar's opening comment in childish scribbling

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the girl's name wraps around the comment

parts.note: Julia is a girl's name
Julius Caesar's boast began veni, vidi, vici, so its first word is veni, I came

explanation.surface: A girl writes Caesar's famous opener among her childhood scribbles.
explanation.walkthrough: Veni, vidi, vici (I came, I saw, I conquered) was Caesar's boast; its opening word sits inside the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Works produced by an author in youth are early writings, often immature.

clue.text: Insect initially likes biting tip of tasty leaf

indicators.note: the insect and its follower bite into something, holding it between their letters

parts.note: a bee is an insect

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter
initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A bug enjoys nibbling the edge of a delicious leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives L from likes and 'tip of' gives T from tasty; 'biting' puts T inside BEE + L.
explanation.definitionFit: The betel is a plant whose leaves are chewed with areca nut in South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Downer, filled with Ecstasy, from under the counter?

indicators.note: the downer's word is filled with a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a blow is a setback, a downer
E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A depressant laced with Ecstasy is sold illicitly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filled with' puts E inside BLOW. 'Under the counter' looks like the illicit sale but literally means lower than the shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To be under a surface is to lie beneath it, lower down.

clue.text: Go live with some recording

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a take is one recorded attempt at a piece, part of a recording session

explanation.surface: Have a go at living with part of a studio session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Betake' is used reflexively: to betake oneself somewhere is to go there.
explanation.definitionFit: To betake oneself is a formal phrase for travelling or making one's way.

clue.text: Source of illumination not substantial around Kentucky

indicators.note: the flimsy word goes around the state's abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: slight means flimsy, not substantial
KY is the postal abbreviation for Kentucky

explanation.surface: A dim light source somewhere in Kentucky.
explanation.walkthrough: KY is the US postal code for Kentucky; 'not substantial' looks like part of the definition but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A window set into a roof lets daylight into a room.

clue.text: Going to sea not initially unwell

indicators.note: the word for voyaging loses its first letter, its initial

parts.note: sailing is going to sea

explanation.surface: Someone who goes to sea feels poorly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' drops the first letter S from SAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick or in poor health is to be off-colour.

clue.text: Become the right size for strenuous rowing — and almost the best!

indicators.note: strenuous rowing is vigorous and choppy, signalling a shake-up of these letters
almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: top means the best

explanation.surface: Hard rowing nearly makes someone the champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strenuous' rearranges ROWING into GROWIN; 'almost' cuts TOP to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A child fills out clothes bought too large, eventually fitting them.
